K1 Main RPL (ESP32-S3, IM69D130 PDM microphone, 2 × 160 LEDs) · before: a6bad318 · AFE2 stage 1: 7ea24446 and a6113aaf on fe/k1-afe2 · measured 10–11 Nov 2026

K1 Audio Front End

A technical account of the level-control path between the microphone and the light effects: what it was, why it could not show a song's sections, the replacement design, and the evidence for each claim. Every number is from the source, the emulator running the real binary, or the bench unit.

1Summary

4 → 1stages that adapt level by themselves: before, and the design target. Stage 1 adds the new one and removes none yet.
0.37 → 1.01dB out per dB in at 0.03 Hz (a 30 s section), old level signal against the product with AFE2. Seven tracks.
1.02 → 2.95loud ÷ breakdown light output on the real unit, stage off then on, same passage, same session. Second edge: 2.04 → 2.93.
10 of 10track × mode cases where both tracking and contrast of the LED output improved (five tracks, modes 22 and 32, real firmware). Off is byte-identical to the previous build.

What was wrong

  • Every adaptive stage is faster than a section. Follower 2 s, AGC 0.49 s, pitch normaliser 10 s. Each divides the signal by its own recent past.
  • The level signal keeps the beats and loses the sections. Its gain is 0.64–1.02 at beat rates (0.5–3.5 Hz) and 0.37 at 0.03 Hz. Every beat peaks at 1.0 whatever the section.
  • The loud guard's sensor is level-free. It reads the normalised envelope, so dense music trips it at any volume: 89–97 % of music lines at room volume.
  • The only clipping is self-inflicted. A ×21.6 gain before a 16-bit clamp, there to survive a 6-bit truncation in the Goertzel input.

What AFE2 does

  • One meter on the raw samples above 110 Hz: section loudness S, 30 ms up, 1.5 s down.
  • One anchor A, the only automatic level control: 3 s up, 60 s down, re-anchoring after 45 s of lasting quiet.
  • One output, how_much = clamp((S/A)^(γ/2), floor, 1), applied to the brightness of both edges for the live path.
  • The fast signals are untouched, so the beat response is the one already approved. Stage 1 is additive; the old stages come out in stages 2–5.

Firmware a6bad318, environment k1_main_rpl_show_bench. Two paths leave the microphone: a waveform path that produces one level number, and a spectrum path that produces 80 bins and 12 pitch classes. A guard senses one path and acts on both.

3Level budget

One axis, two scales. The microphone's sensitivity (−36 dBFS at 94 dB SPL, ±1 dB) fixes 0 dBFS at 130 dB SPL. Above the line: what physically exists. Below it: thresholds the old firmware put in the way.

4Time scales and transfer

A stage that divides a signal by its own envelope is a high-pass on the signal's level: changes slower than the envelope's release are removed. The question for each stage is where that corner sits against the music.

5AFE2 design

Per hop of N raw samples, Δt = N / fs

y[n] = b0·x[n] + z1 z1 = b1·x[n] − a1·y[n] + z2 z2 = b2·x[n] − a2·y[n] e = (1/N) · Σ y[n]² S ← S + α_S·(e − S) α_S = α(30 ms) if e > S else α(1.5 s) A ← A + α_A·(S − A) α_A = α(3 s) if S > A α(4 s) if re-anchoring α(60 s) otherwise A ← max(A, 36) how = clamp((S / A)^(γ/2), floor, 1) α(τ) = 1 − exp(−Δt / τ)

S and A are energies in raw counts². With γ = 1, how_much is the ratio of sound pressures, √(S/A).

ElementDefinitionValueα at 7.5 msWhy this value
High-pass2nd-order Butterworth, RBJ biquad, transposed direct form II110 Hz, Q 0.7071 · b = [0.962538, -1.925077, 0.962538] · a = [1, -1.923673, 0.926481]The plate shows nothing below its lowest bin; room rumble must not set the reference. 50 Hz is down 13.9 dB in the meter only; the beat signal still hears it.
Section loudness SS ← S + α (e − S), α by directionτ 30 ms ↑ · 1.5 s ↓0.2212 ↑ · 0.00499 ↓30 ms equals the old follower's attack, so a drop lands on its first beat. 1.5 s is close to the 3 s short-term window of EBU R128.
Anchor A, risingA ← A + α (S − A) when S > Aτ 3 s0.00250A louder room or passage becomes the reference in seconds. Hearing-aid AGCs lower gain about three times faster than they raise it (ADRO: 9 dB/s against 3 dB/s).
Anchor A, holdingA ← A + α (S − A) when S ≤ Aτ 60 s0.0001250.07 dB/s recovery: a 30 s breakdown at −10 dB is still shown at 0.40 when it ends. Sections last 15–60 s.
Anchor A, re-anchoringsame update with a faster α after S < A/4 for 45 s, until S > 0.7 Aτ 4 s · hold 45 s · ratios 0.25, 0.700.00187A quieter programme that lasts is not a breakdown. Dual-loop idea from Moore and Glasberg's hearing-aid AGC: slow loop normally, fast action only on a lasting change.
Anchor floorA ≥ A_min36 counts² (6 counts rms)Measured quiet room above 110 Hz: 1.1 counts rms. Music quieter than 6 counts is shown proportionally smaller, never amplified.
Maphow_much = clamp((S/A)^(γ/2), floor, 1)γ 1.0 · floor 0.25 (runtime)γ 1 gives 0.5 dB of luminance per dB of sound. Matching loudness to brightness needs 0.6–1.0 (Stevens and Marks 1965), i.e. γ 1.2–2. Left at 1 for the first look; set on the plate.

The loop body as committed (audio/k1_afe2.cpp)

  float z1 = st.z1, z2 = st.z2, acc = 0.0f;
  for (uint16_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    const float x = (float)raw[i];
    const float y = st.b0 * x + z1;
    z1 = st.b1 * x - st.a1 * y + z2;
    z2 = st.b2 * x - st.a2 * y;
    acc += y * y;
  }
  if (!isfinite(z1) || !isfinite(z2) || !isfinite(acc)) {   // never let one bad hop poison the state
    z1 = 0.0f;
    z2 = 0.0f;
    acc = 0.0f;
  }
  st.z1 = z1;
  st.z2 = z2;
  const float e = acc / (float)count;

  st.section += ((e > st.section) ? st.a_s_attack : st.a_s_release) * (e - st.section);

  if (st.section > st.anchor) {
    st.anchor += st.a_a_up * (st.section - st.anchor);
    st.quiet_s = 0.0f;
    st.fast = false;
  } else {
    if (st.section < K1_AFE2_QUIET_RATIO * st.anchor) {
      st.quiet_s += dt_s;
      if (st.quiet_s > K1_AFE2_HOLD_S) st.fast = true;
    } else {
      st.quiet_s = 0.0f;
    }
    if (st.fast && st.section > K1_AFE2_FAST_EXIT_RATIO * st.anchor) st.fast = false;
    st.anchor += (st.fast ? st.a_a_fast : st.a_a_slow) * (st.section - st.anchor);
  }
  if (!(st.anchor >= K1_AFE2_ANCHOR_MIN)) st.anchor = K1_AFE2_ANCHOR_MIN;

6Behaviour

The compiled firmware module, driven with 100 s of broadband noise whose level is stepped: full, −10 dB for 10 s, full, −14 dB for 70 s, silence, full.

Known behaviours that follow from the design

  • The first quiet intro after power-on is shown at full. The anchor starts at its floor and has nothing louder to compare with.
  • A build that only gets louder is shown at full throughout, since the anchor follows a rise in 3 s. Growth shows only against something louder heard in the last minute or so.
  • Turning the volume down dims the plate for up to 45 s, then it recovers in about 10 s.
  • Sparse loud hits in a quiet passage read as loud for about 1.5 s each: S has a 30 ms attack. That is intended (the light is the sound), and it lowers contrast for such passages.
  • how_much updates at 133 Hz and is read at 100 Hz without synchronisation. One float; a torn read is not possible on this CPU.

7Interactive model

The same update as the firmware, running in this page on the seven tracks. Move a control and the result is recomputed.

Dashed blue in the top panel is the anchor. The model runs at 10 samples per second for size; the firmware runs at 133. Against the full-rate reference its how_much differs by 0.033 on average. The JavaScript equals the Python reference on the same samples to 5e-06. It models the level signal, not what an effect draws.

Hypotheses that were tested and failed

HypothesisTestObservedVerdict
Scaling the published level makes quiet sections smaller in every modeEmulator, :k1_afe on the level path, modes 22, 32, 18Mode 22 as predicted. Mode 32 and 18: breakdown brightness rose 0.028 → 0.048 and 0.027 → 0.044, because those modes map a lower level to wider bands and longer trails.Refuted. The factor moved to output brightness; level scaling kept as a separate switch.
The dark stretch in mode 22's loud chorus is caused by the pitch sparseness gateEmulator, vp_chroma_gate=false, guard on and offBrightness in the stretch 0.0063 → 0.0069; zero lit pixels while E = 0.83–0.99.Refuted. The mode draws only on the positive side of its own oscillator.
The loud guard causes the flat responseEmulator, guard on against off, two passages, three modesMode 22 final chorus +25 %; chorus-to-quiet ratio below 1 with the guard on or off.Partly. The guard squashes chorus hits; the missing section term is a separate cause.
The old level signal carries no section informationCross-spectral gain on seven tracksIt keeps 0.37 dB per dB at 0.03 Hz, through how densely peaks arrive, not through their height.Refuted as stated. Every beat still peaks at 1.0 in every section.

11Science and prior art

FindingNumberSourceConsequence here
Cochlear compression0.2–0.3 dB out per dB in near best frequency, 40–90 dB SPL, effectively instantaneousRobles and Ruggero 2001A static curve, not a time-averaged gain. Level differences are squeezed, never removed.
Adaptation to mean levelshifts the coding range by 0.05–0.47 dB per dB (mean 0.25–0.34); 160 ms after a rise, 330 ms after a fall, plus tens of secondsDean et al. 2005, 2008; Wen et al. 2009Hearing cancels about a third of a lasting level change. The old chain cancels about two thirds at section rates and, in the spectrum path, more.
Loudness scale+10 dB sounds twice as loud; windows of 400 ms, 3 s and the whole programmeITU-R BS.1770, EBU R128, Tech 3342S uses a release near the 3 s window.
Brightness scale and matchingbrightness ∝ luminance^0.33 (extended source) to ^0.5 (point); matched to loudness at about the same exponent on energyStevens and Marks 19650.6–1.0 dB of luminance per dB of sound; γ 1.2–2.
Music's level modulationbroad peak near 2 Hz across 39 hours of recordingsDing et al. 2017Beats sit at 0.5–4 Hz: the old level signal passes these, and AFE2 leaves them to it.
Recognition front endsPCEN at defaults removes about 98 % of a sustained level change; RASTA removes changes slower than about 1 HzWang et al. 2017; Lostanlen et al. 2019; HermanskyRight for detectors, wrong for a display of dynamics.
Dual-loop AGCslow loop sets level; fast loop acts only on a jump of more than about 8 dB; gain held in pausesMoore and Glasberg 1988; Stone et al. 1999; Moore 2008The anchor's three states.
Microphone−36 dBFS at 94 dB SPL (±1 dB); overload 130 dB SPL; 1 % distortion at 128 dB SPL; noise 25–29 dB(A)Infineon IM69D130 datasheet, Table 10 dBFS = 130 dB SPL. Nothing in a venue clips it.

No system surveyed is shown to keep a drop brighter than a breakdown while also adapting to the room unattended. The firmware's own comments call the four-band AGC a pre-fork "Sensory Bridge cochlear AGC"; no upstream release contains one, so it originated in this fork line. The hearing-science label is also inaccurate: the cochlea compresses instantly and does not normalise.

Open parameters

  • γ. 1.0 as flashed (0.5 dB/dB). Research supports 1.2–2. Set by eye on the plate.
  • floor. 0.25 (−6 dB luminance). Sets how alive a breakdown and an idle room look.
  • τ slow, hold time. 60 s and 45 s. A 90 s ambient breakdown brightens after 45 s.
  • Anchor floor. 6 counts against a measured 1.1-count room. Could go lower for very quiet listening.
  • Where else to apply how_much. Level scaling is right for mode 22's shapes and wrong for mode 32's width. Per-effect use is open.

Limits of the evidence

  • LED evidence covers five tracks and two modes in the emulator; three of the five are electronic. The bench uses one track.
  • One breakdown-to-return transition per track; 22 enabled modes exist and two were measured on five tracks, three on one.
  • The bench A/B is two consecutive plays of one passage at −10 dB, not a simultaneous comparison.
  • The Captain's eye has not judged it. That is the acceptance test, and no measurement here replaces it.
  • dB SPL figures assume unity gain in the PDM converter.
  • The transfer measurement treats a non-linear, clamped system as linear; read it as a describing gain.
  • Until stages 2–5 land the unit runs five self-adjusting stages.
